## Statistical inference (chapter)

There are two main two **main topics** in *statistical inference*:

* Confidence interval
* Hypothesis testing

You can read about them [in the script by Dr Kochański](https://blazejkochanski-statystyka2.share.connect.posit.cloud/). 

### Confidence interval (sub-chapter)

A __confidence interval__ is a range of values used to estimate an unknown population parameter. It is constructed in such a way that, under appropriate conditions, there is a specified probability -- called the __confidence level__ -- that the interval calculated based on a random sample will contain the true parameter value.

The confidence level is typically expressed as a percentage. Typical confidence levels: 90%, 95%, 99%. 

**Example 1:**

1. A producer of a medicinal skin cream is interested in the proportion of people of a certain age for whom the cream will improve their skin condition. In a random sample of 68 people, a positive effect was observed in 42 cases. What proportion of people can be expected to see an improvement with this cream, with 99% confidence, in the population?

```{r}
# install.packages("binom")
binom::binom.confint(42, 68, 
                     conf.level = 0.99, 
                     method = "asymptotic")

```

**Example 2:**

Randomly select 100 locations on Earth, checking whether you land on water or land. Based on this, estimate the proportion of land on Earth's surface. Assume a 90% confidence interval.

[Sampling tool](https://bankonomia.nazwa.pl/globe/)

Input your results [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TCaPAH1D51l5j0A4WauehP22m8zyww7n8eLQcjGBpEw/edit?usp=sharing).

```{r}
binom::binom.confint(34, 100, 
                     conf.level = 0.9, 
                     method = "asymptotic")

```

**Example 3:**

Determine the 99-percent confidence intervals for the average travel time of dr. B by bicycle on the route between the university and home based on sample data:

* for any trip,
* for the trip to the university,
* for the return trip from the university.

Data can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MvyoGcPtW3hUa4iARd2RLM6ahfMBFBYqfzet3K9_6do/edit?gid=1150951672#gid=1150951672).

```{r}
URL = "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MvyoGcPtW3hUa4iARd2RLM6ahfMBFBYqfzet3K9_6do/edit?gid=1150951672#gid=1150951672"
library(googlesheets4)
gs4_deauth()
data <- read_sheet(URL)
time_total <- as.numeric(data$czas)
hist(time_total)
```

* for any trip,
```{r}
round(mean(time_total),2)
round(sd(time_total),2)
round(length(time_total),2)

test_result<-t.test(time_total, conf.level = 0.99)
print(test_result$conf.int)
```

* for the trip to the university,
```{r}
test_result<-t.test(time_total[data$kierunek=="naPG"], conf.level = 0.99)
print(test_result$conf.int)
```

* for the return trip from the university.
```{r}
test_result<-t.test(time_total[data$kierunek=="zPG"], conf.level = 0.99)
print(test_result$conf.int)
```
